henry: Quick proposal: tighten SIEM export retention + access for third-party consumers. idea: streaming sinks stay 30 days, batch exports to partner buckets default 7 days, require per-export RBAC tags + KMS envelope key, and audit tokens for downloads. thoughts?
tara: +1. can you explain partner bucket TTL vs internal SIEM TTL?
henry: internal SIEM (splunk/elasticsearch) retains raw event indexes for 90d by policy. partner exports are copies we push to external buckets — lower retention to reduce exposure and cost.
josh: how do we enforce RBAC on S3-style buckets? we already have bucket policies but partners occasionally request wildcard access.
henry: plan is: per-export service account + presigned short-lived URLs, no long-lived creds. all downloads require an export token tied to a ticket. token expires after 1h and is logged.
sec-bot: SECURITY BOT: recommended controls: 1) per-export CMK wrap 2) presigned URLs TTL <=1h 3) export manifest with sample hashes 4) RBAC attribute tag: export:partner=<id>
henry: KMS detail: use envelope encryption. per-export DEK wrapped with platform CMK, and add an access-policy tag that limits unwrap to the KMS-proxy role. unwraps require requestor+approver recorded.
tara: legal ask: what about subpoenas/legal hold? if legal hold needed, partner copy must be frozen; don't allow auto-deletion.
legal: correct. any export subject to legal hold must be flagged; auto-delete suppressed and retention admins notified. legal hold requests create HOOKED-HOLD tickets as earlier.
josh: operational: for streaming sinks we sometimes sample to save downstream cost; does sampling affect evidentiary exports?
henry: yes. exports for compliance/evidence must be unsampled. add a flag sample=false to manifest. otherwise sampling allowed.
nora: can we add metadata to exports so we can revoke partner access and rotate keys if a leak suspected?
henry: include revoke_id in the manifest; revocation will trigger KMS key rotation for that export's wrap key and invalidate presigned URLs.
sec-bot: SECURITY BOT: new export request template published https://internal.redwood/exports/new. required fields: ticket, partner_id, scope, ttl_hours, sample_flag, approvers.
tara: can you paste a quick example CLI request? i'll add it to our runbook.
henry: sure:
```
rdw export create --ticket RDW-4567 --partner acme-corp --scope "service-b:2026-03-19T00:00..2026-03-19T06:00" --ttl 168 --sample false --kms-wrap platform-cmk --approvers sec-lead,privacy
```
josh: nit: TTL default should be small, maybe 168h (7d) for partner buckets; we might allow 30d for vetted partners via contract.
legal: contract exceptions allowed but need documented data processing addendum and security attestation.
nora: monitoring: let's emit telemetry: export.created, export.downloaded, unwrap.requested, unwrap.approved, export.revoked. attach to token id.
henry: agree. also propose an alert: >5 unique IP downloads for same export in 1h => suspicious.
tara: can we require data minimization for partners? e.g., redact user identifiers unless contractually necessary.
henry: yes. add scrub presets: minimal (PII removed), standard (IP hashed), full (no scrub, high-approval). partners must declare required fields and justify.
sec-bot: SECURITY BOT: enforcement notes: policy engine will reject export requests lacking ticket or approvers, or ttl >720h without legal flag.
legal: final note: any export crossing region boundaries needs privacy review.
henry: thanks. i'll draft a short RFC and add the template + runbook snippets. filing RFC now.
tara: thanks — i'll help with runbook tests. :white_check_mark:
